staleness_note: This file deliberately carries no timestamp: a clock here would make every sync commit a file whose only change is the time. Read `generated_at` from `.colaberry/manifest.json` and label it "last changed", not "last checked".

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: An agent must never set or raise its own authority, which charter boundary 8 states directly. R2 caps it at reporting the record from approved knowledge. This capability exists to make the absence of an approved level visible rather than to grant one.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This is the capability that puts curriculum in front of learners, so it is human-decided forever and effectiveAuthority() caps it at autonomy:R5. Even R5 is shadow only: the agent prepares a publish packet and a named human publishes. Reaching real students additionally needs push_to_protected_main and production_deploy, both default-denied, so no automation rung is reachable at all.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A weight or domain change propagates into every student's readiness score and into what the prep bank must cover, so the change is permanently human-required. R2 is the ceiling because the input - what Anthropic currently publishes - cannot be agent-verified: it needs a human-confirmed source, and an unbounded network fetch is default-denied.

A pure read-only audit over the whole bank with no write path, so R7 is permitted for producing the audit. Withdrawing or regenerating a failing bank is a separate human decision because it changes the material students practise on.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Proposing a mapping has no effect until a human verifies it, but the verified mapping changes a student's readiness score, so the decision is permanently human-required and capped at autonomy:R5. Proposal is the agent's whole role; setting a state is not available at any rung.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Approving an assessment item is exactly the human decision this matrix protects, and it reaches learners directly. R2 is the ceiling rather than R5 because the agent has no legitimate role beyond answering from approved knowledge and recommending: a shadow comparison against human approvals would normalise an agent opinion on whether an item is fit to serve.

Scoring, triaging and drafting a candidate are read-only and provably write-free, which makes producing the review one nameable action class and R7 permissible. Persisting a revision or changing its status is a different capability and is human-decided. This capability touches preparation material only and nothing about it issues a credential.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Charter boundary 4 makes this manager-authored only, permanently: the agent may report against its own KPIs but may never approve them, and boundary 8 forbids it changing its own autonomy level. R2 is therefore the ceiling - answering from approved knowledge - and no higher rung is coherent for a capability whose whole point is that a human holds the pen.

Reporting readiness is a computation over existing records with no learner-facing change and no credential effect, so R7 is permitted for producing the report. Acting on a weak cohort - changing what is taught or what is practised - is a separate human decision.

Pure read-only detection with a stable output and no side effect, so R7 is permitted for reporting the gap list. Filling a gap is excluded from this capability because it would change what a student is taught.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: The curate half is a read-only proposal, but the apply half puts third-party content in front of learners, which makes the capability human-decided and caps it at autonomy:R5. The agent's role ends at the proposal; applying needs the publish path, which itself needs default-denied capabilities.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Scope is a governance boundary and an agent must never be able to widen its own. R2 caps it at reporting from the approved contract. Charter boundary 5 forbids silently absorbing a deferred or out-of-scope item at any rung, so no higher level exists for this capability by design.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: The assessment is read-only, but it exists to gate a change that reaches learners mid-programme, which makes it human-decided and caps it at autonomy:R5. At R5 the agent produces the assessment and a human decides; applying the change is a different capability and needs default-denied capabilities to reach production.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Generating a recommendation has no side effect, but the recommendation is about what a student is taught, which makes the decision permanently human-required and caps the capability at autonomy:R5 under effectiveAuthority(). The apply step is deliberately excluded: an agent may propose a patch and never apply one.

Genuinely read-only: the ticket write was deliberately removed and a test asserts zero tickets. R7 is permitted because producing this one report is a single explicitly nameable action class with no side effect. R8 and R9 are withheld: no handoff recipient exists and no monitoring or recovery story has been written for it.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Approval is the gate between a draft and something a student can be scheduled into, so it is permanently human-required and capped at autonomy:R5. Even at R5 the agent only prepares the promotion diff. Promotion itself needs push_to_protected_main and production_deploy, both default-denied, so there is no automation path.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A type definition determines the shape of a learning activity, so it is human-decided. R4 permits stateful multi-step draft authoring in sandbox, which is genuinely where this work lives. R5 is withheld because the preview is a lower-fidelity approximation of the real student card, so a shadow comparison would be measuring the wrong artifact.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: An autonomy ceiling over an undefined scope would be a fabrication. autonomy:R0 is deliberately the lowest ceiling in this matrix and stays there until a human interview produces the duty list. R0 is itself the work: define the workflow, the risks and the human decisions.

Internal queue write about readiness, not a credential decision and not learner-facing. R6 is the ceiling for the same reason as the curriculum flag: it already writes in production, so the honest next rung is a separately approved supervised pilot. No issuance of any kind is in scope at any rung.

An internal queue write a human must act on, not a learner-facing change. R6 (separately approved supervised production pilot) is the ceiling because it already writes in production and the honest next step is a supervised pilot with a named approver, not automation. R7 is withheld: no action class has been explicitly authorized on this ladder.

Delivering a finding to a named human is not itself a decision about what students are taught, so it is not human_decision. R6 caps it at a separately approved supervised pilot because the delivery is a real external side effect and the designed email channel is both unbuilt and, as live_email, default-denied to an agent.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: The decision is a human one and it affects a student's record and progression, so it is permanently human-required. R4 permits the agent to do the stateful preparation work - reading the file, laying out the claim - in sandbox, but no rung lets it approve, and nothing here issues a credential at any rung.

The audit itself only reads call sites and event records, so R7 is permitted for producing the inventory. Remediating a path - giving it an identity, a switch, or turning it off - changes what students read and is a human decision handled elsewhere.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Producing the finding is read-only, but the finding exists to inform a change to what students are taught, which makes the decision permanently human-required. R4 permits the stateful multi-step analysis in sandbox; R5 is withheld because no approved reference finding set exists to shadow against, and a drop-off cannot yet be separated from its cause.

Reading call sites and cost events and reporting them has no side effect, so R7 is permitted for producing the report. Changing a call site to add an identity is a code change with its own review, and is excluded here.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Who may reach and decide for an AI employee is a governance decision for a human, and an agent reporting on its own access must never be able to affect it. R2 caps it at answering from approved knowledge; granting access is excluded at every rung, consistent with the rule that manager instructions may only restrict an agent.

Answering the manager's own questions in her own thread has no side effect and no learner contact, so R7 is permitted for that one action class. It is nonetheless not at R7 today: nothing has been approved, and a successful conversation is explicitly not evidence of promotion.

A real external write under a shared credential that misattributes authorship to a named person is the highest-consequence thing in this domain that is not learner-facing. R5 caps it at shadow comparison until the credential question Ali flagged as unresolved is actually resolved; R6 would require that resolution plus a separate pilot approval.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Drafting is not publishing, so the drafting work itself can reach stateful multi-step sandbox tasks. It stops at autonomy:R4 rather than R5 because the output is curriculum a learner would be taught, which makes it a permanently human-required decision, and because the preconditions that make its write path safe are unmet: a shadow comparison against a reference outcome would be measuring a loop that still leaves partial writes.

It does not decide what a student is taught, so it is not a human_decision capability; but it writes a real external Basecamp side effect at risk tier R3, so automation is withheld and R6 (separately approved supervised pilot) is the ceiling. R8 is explicitly unavailable: no second AI employee has a matching capability to hand off to.

Running the gate is pure, deterministic and side-effect-free: it reads a plan and returns checks. R7 is permitted for that one authorized action class, reporting the result. Acting on the result - publishing anyway over a warn - is a separate capability and is human-decided.

One write to the agent's own row, affecting nobody else's data and conveying no curriculum. R7 is permitted for that single authorized action class. R9 is withheld because no monitoring, recovery or ownership story exists for it: the signal is content-free and a failure is indistinguishable from idleness.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A proposal to change what Colaberry teaches is a human decision at every level, which effectiveAuthority() treats as permanently human-required. R2 is the ceiling rather than R5 because the capability has no approval path at all today: until a human can actually adopt or decline a proposal, anything above answering from approved knowledge would manufacture work that cannot be acted on, which is precisely the 175-cancelled-initiative failure mode.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This reaches a learner and conveys curriculum content, so what it says is a human decision and effectiveAuthority() caps a human_decision capability at autonomy:R5 (autonomyLadder.ts:169-173). It already runs unsupervised in production, which is a finding rather than a justification: a passing conversation proves nothing and cannot promote it.

It writes per-student internal tasks a human acts on and never contacts the learner, so it is not itself a human_decision capability. R6 is the ceiling because it already runs in production against real student data and the honest next rung is a separately approved supervised pilot, not automation of an unmeasured flag.

Detection is read-only but the alert fan-out is a real production side effect with named recipients, and RISK_REGISTER.md:16 rates that fan-out as high impact if absorbed carelessly. R6 therefore caps it at a separately approved supervised pilot. Replacing a broken video is excluded from this capability entirely because it would alter live curriculum.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A blueprint is the declaration of what a week teaches, so its content is a human decision and is permanently human-required. R4 permits stateful multi-step authoring of drafts in sandbox; R5 is withheld because there is no approved reference blueprint set to shadow against, and inventing one would be the fabrication this matrix exists to avoid.

A read-only inventory over repository content with no write path, so R7 is permitted for producing the report. Editing any of this content is publishing to learners, which is excluded from this capability entirely and would additionally need push_to_protected_main and production_deploy, both default-denied.

authority_rule.rule: A capability approved above autonomy:R2 with no granted tools is forced back down to autonomy:R2, with the reason no_tool_grants. Tool grants are the throttle.
authority_rule.note: When this binds nothing, say so in words. It means no capability in this domain has been approved above autonomy:R2 yet, not that the rule is absent or that the panel failed.

governance.disclosure: A filed request grants nothing. Status is what a named human decided, and a pending row means nobody has decided yet.

verification.disclosure: A criterion counts as passing when it is marked in `.colaberry/progress.json` in this repository. The verifier reads that file on every sync and records what it found. A story showing 0 of N is not a rejection: nothing has been claimed yet.
